vo_natural_dune_stoss_slope.evidence: At 512x288 thumbnail scale, the dominant connected dune has a broad, gently rising left stoss surface that is visibly longer and shallower than the compact right lee face.

vo_natural_dune_crest.evidence: At thumbnail and 1672x941 native scale, one narrow continuous ridge runs from the lower-right foreground toward the upper center and visibly separates the two dune faces.

vo_natural_dune_slipface.evidence: At both scales, a darker, smooth, steep lee slip face descends immediately to the right of that same continuous crest.

vo_natural_dune_ripples.evidence: Native pixels show many fine, parallel ripple and saltation traces aligned across the broad stoss surface and bending consistently toward the crest.

vo_natural_dune_non_inference.evidence: Native pixels show a single connected asymmetric sand body with unequal slopes, shared crest, aligned ripples, and low drifting grains; the reading is not carried by a symmetric pile, flat texture, or dust cloud alone, and no numerical wind-speed or migration-rate claim is made.
